consensus_summary: Across all four blind responses the settled core is that 'life'/'the life' symbolizes eternal, divine life (zōē) given by God through Jesus Christ, with the definite form widely functioning as a christological title — Christ himself as the embodiment and source of that life (John 14:6; 11:25; 1:4; 1 John 5:11-12). A Deuteronomic 'covenant blessing / choose life' reading appears only as a common secondary alternative, not the core.
book_summary: The book defines 'the life' as covenant existence — a manner of living, walking in the Way according to God's law (Deut 30:19-20; Lev 18:5; Matt 7:14) — and explicitly flags the common teaching ('Christ Himself, and the eternal life imparted to believers') as the view it departs from.
consensus_core_identification: 'The life' = eternal/divine life in and through Christ, and Christ himself as its personal embodiment and source.
book_core_identification: 'The life' = covenant existence: the ongoing walk of obedience to God's law along the Way.
boundary_disagreement: The book excludes the christological-title and imparted-eternal-life senses from the core and reclassifies the key Johannine proof text (John 14:6) as referring to a law-ordered covenant walk rather than to Christ's person as source of divine life. It retains the Deuteronomic/Levitical covenant cases (Deut 30:19-20; Lev 18:5) that the consensus treats as secondary, elevating them to the center.
material_contradiction: The consensus identifies 'the life' as Christ himself and the eternal life he imparts; the book's common-view note names exactly that identification and replaces it with covenant existence lived by obedience to God's law. A person (and a divinely imparted gift) and a human mode of law-observant living are different referents; accepting the book's core requires rejecting the consensus identification for the same passages (e.g., John 14:6).
rationale: This is not mere narrowing within the consensus category: the book substitutes a different central referent (obedient covenant living) for the consensus referent (Christ/eternal divine life), and its own note marks the consensus view as the 'commonly taught' position it corrects. The book's reading does correspond to a listed consensus alternative (the covenantal-choice reading in Response A, covenant flourishing in Response C), so it is not NOVEL; but promoting that alternative to displace the christological/eternal-life core, including reinterpreting John 14:6, constitutes replacement, hence DIVERGENT. Extensionally there is partial reclassification: Deuteronomic cases are shared, while the Johannine texts are reassigned a different sense.
strongest_objection: One could argue REFINED: 'covenant life' is already a recognized common alternative within the consensus, and Deut 30:20 ('he is thy life') even links life to God himself, so the book might be seen as re-weighting emphasis within the same broad salvific category rather than replacing the referent. But the book's explicit contrast with the common christological/eternal-life teaching, and its reinterpretation of John 14:6 away from Christ-as-life toward a law-walk, tips this to replacement rather than boundary adjustment.
